turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity, which pulls on Earth’s oceans and creates bulges of water on opposite sides of the planet. The Sun’s gravity also influences tides, though less strongly. As Earth rotates, coastlines move through these bulges, producing high and low tides. The shape of coastlines and ocean depths affect local timing and height of tides. Understanding tides helps explain coastal patterns, navigation, fishing, and marine ecosystems. Tides follow predictable cycles but vary by location and seasonal factors.
